hypothesis: hir-def's name resolution (DefMap, item scopes, use-import fixed point, module files, block scopes, extern prelude) resolves Rust path calls to their function from source alone, inside the never-rustc boundary
blocking_question_resolved: the corpus question (a bounded slice of name resolution that moves CALL observations off UNRESOLVED without crossing the never-rustc/full-resolution boundary) is answered yes: path calls, resolved by module/import rules only; method calls need hir-ty inference and stay out
primary_sources: crates/hir-def/src/nameres/collector.rs (import fixed point, glob propagation, shadowing)

cheapest_falsification.method: on Atlas's own workspace, resolve every path call natively and compare each resolution with the pinned rust-analyzer 1.90.0 SCIP index at the same anchor
cheapest_falsification.misses_are_sound_refusals: unresolved-import/associated-not-found: macro-generated items (core::identity typed_id!) and derived impls (#[derive(Default)]) the pass does not expand; local-binding: a binding of the same name anywhere in the function (conservative); ambiguous: a cfg alternate
cheapest_falsification.defect_found_by_the_oracle: a block-level `use super::super::tests::element` was mis-resolved: chained `super` was not honoured and the unresolved import let the lookup fall through to the enclosing module's glob; fixed (chained super; an unresolvable named import binds its name as unknown) before promotion

absorbed_mechanism.name: hir-def-path-resolution
absorbed_mechanism.native_owner: adapter::semantic::rust::resolve (DefMap, fixed point, path resolution) + runtime::census::resolution (engine atlas.resolution.rust-paths, observing the syntactic CALL claims)
deviations: conflicting globs are AMBIGUOUS (hir-def keeps the first); never a pick
a lookup in a scope with item macros or an unresolvable glob is OPEN and never falls through
a local binding of the name anywhere in the function blocks resolution (hir-def scopes lets after their initializer)
Type::assoc uses inherent impls, then trait impls of the concrete type (hir-ty's probe reduced to unique-name lookup)

REFERENCE_ONLY: hir-ty type inference and method resolution (needed for the 11,704 method calls; full trait solving, far beyond a bounded absorption -- the pinned rust-analyzer binary remains the verification oracle, EXTERNAL_BOUNDARY via rust #14)
macro expansion, proc macros, salsa-backed IDE queries, base-db/project-model (the Cargo dependency census already owns the crate graph)
